skill.name: dingtalk-bridge
skill.description: Bridge Claude Code or Codex workflows with DingTalk group chats. It sends markdown or text messages, runs a Stream bot for mentions, and can post AI replies back to the group.
skill.summary: Send DingTalk messages and run a group chat bridge for AI coding workflows.
skill.author: mguozhen

security_audit.summary: Most documentation and test alerts are false positives, and the DingTalk network calls are expected for this bridge. The serious risk is that the Stream bot can execute DingTalk group messages through Claude Code with permissions bypassed, while the installer can add persistence. Automatic publication should wait for authorization, approval, and least-privilege safeguards.

remediation.issue: Remote chat messages execute Claude Code without approval.
remediation.suggestion: Remove --dangerously-skip-permissions by default, add sender and group allowlists, require an explicit command prefix, and support human approval before running prompts.

remediation.issue: The bot can be installed as a persistent macOS LaunchAgent.
remediation.suggestion: Make persistence a separate manual setup step with clear unload instructions, logging guidance, and least-privilege service account recommendations.

remediation.issue: The Claude subprocess inherits the full process environment.
remediation.suggestion: Pass a minimal environment to the child process and avoid exposing DingTalk credentials or unrelated secrets to prompt-driven execution.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted DingTalk Mentions Execute With Permissions Bypassed
semantic_findings.description: The Stream bot takes nonempty DingTalk group mention text and runs it through the Claude CLI with --dangerously-skip-permissions. A chat participant could cause file or command actions in the configured workdir.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The handler extracts chat text and starts execute_prompt, and execute_prompt passes that text to claude -p with --dangerously-skip-permissions. The README also documents receiving mentions and auto-executing them.

semantic_findings.title: No Authorization Gate Before Running Group Messages
semantic_findings.description: The message handler starts execution for any nonempty callback text after saving conversation metadata. I found no sender allowlist, group allowlist, approval step, or command prefix check before execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The control flow shows text is extracted and immediately used to start execute_prompt in a daemon thread. No authorization or approval condition appears in the handler.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Dependencies Installed During Setup
semantic_findings.description: The installer fetches dingtalk_stream and websockets without version pins or hash verification. Future package changes could alter installed behavior during setup.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The install command names dependencies without versions or hashes. This is a clear supply-chain risk, although it does not show malicious intent by itself.

content.user_title: Connect AI Coding Agents to DingTalk
content.value_statement: Teams need a direct way to share AI coding updates in DingTalk. This skill sends messages, listens for group mentions, and returns AI responses to the same chat.
actual_capabilities: Send markdown messages to a configured DingTalk group through OpenAPI.
Send plain text notifications to the same group conversation.
Run a DingTalk Stream listener that receives group mentions.
Save conversation metadata from DingTalk callbacks for later sends.
Invoke the configured Claude CLI from incoming chat text and post the result.
Create local configuration and an optional macOS LaunchAgent during setup.
limitations: Requires a DingTalk enterprise app with Robot and Stream mode enabled.
The Stream bot can execute prompts from chat, so it should only run in trusted groups.
The default conversation file stores one active conversation unless configured differently.
macOS persistence uses LaunchAgent; Linux service setup must be created separately.

use_cases.title: Send Release Updates
use_cases.description: Post build, test, and deployment status to a DingTalk group from an AI coding session.

use_cases.title: Answer Team Requests
use_cases.description: Let trusted teammates mention the bot and receive AI-generated project responses in the group chat.

use_cases.title: Prototype Internal Chat Automation
use_cases.description: Use DingTalk Stream and OpenAPI examples to build a small internal assistant workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Send A Simple Update
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner notification from the current project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Send a DingTalk message to the configured group: The staging deploy is complete.

prompt_templates.title: Send A Markdown Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Formatted status update for a team channel.
prompt_templates.prompt: Send a DingTalk markdown message titled Daily Build Report with today's test status and blockers.

prompt_templates.title: Start The Stream Bot
prompt_templates.scenario: Interactive setup check before receiving group mentions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my DingTalk Bridge configuration, then start the Stream bot for this project and explain any missing credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Review Bot Safety
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before enabling automatic chat execution.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project before enabling DingTalk Bridge auto execution. Identify who can trigger it, what workdir it uses, and what safeguards are missing.

output_examples.input: Send a DingTalk message that the deploy is complete.
output_examples.output: A plain notification is posted to the configured DingTalk group, and the terminal reports that the message was sent.

output_examples.input: Mention the Stream bot in DingTalk and ask for open blockers.
output_examples.output: The bot acknowledges the request, runs the configured AI CLI in the project directory, and replies with a concise markdown summary.

output_examples.input: Ask for a daily build report with test results and next steps.
output_examples.output: The group receives a titled markdown report that includes status, blockers, and suggested follow-up actions.

best_practices: Keep DingTalk credentials in environment variables or a permission-restricted config file.
Run the Stream bot only in trusted groups with clear ownership and monitoring.
Use a least-privileged work directory and review prompts before enabling automatic execution.
anti_patterns: Do not expose the Stream bot to broad groups or untrusted chat participants.
Do not run the LaunchAgent on sensitive workstations without monitoring and an unload plan.
Do not commit DingTalk app secrets or conversation metadata to shared repositories.

faq.question: What DingTalk setup is required?
faq.answer: You need a DingTalk enterprise internal app with Robot capability and Stream message mode enabled.

faq.question: Can it send both markdown and plain text?
faq.answer: Yes. The send module supports markdown messages with a title and plain text notifications.

faq.question: Can it receive DingTalk messages?
faq.answer: Yes. The Stream bot listens for group mentions and can reply through DingTalk.

faq.question: Where are credentials stored?
faq.answer: Credentials can come from environment variables or config.json. Protect the app secret like any other production token.

faq.question: Does this work with Codex?
faq.answer: Codex can operate the Python commands, but the Stream execution path invokes the Claude CLI by default unless reconfigured.

faq.question: Is automatic execution safe?
faq.answer: It is only suitable for trusted environments. Add allowlists, approval gates, and least-privilege settings before persistent use.
